analysis.one_liner: Eicher Motors makes premium motorcycles under the Royal Enfield brand and co-owns VECV, a commercial vehicle joint venture with Volvo.
analysis.whats_happening: Q2 FY27 results are due on 28 October 2026, just five days from today. The last reported quarter (Q1 FY27, June 2026) was strong on the Royal Enfield side with record volumes, but the company is also navigating a GST change: tax on motorcycles up to 350cc was cut to 18% (helping the bulk of Royal Enfield's volumes), while bikes above 350cc now attract a flat 40% GST, up from an effective ~31% earlier - that hits the premium models (Himalayan 450, Interceptor, Super Meteor, the newly launched Bullet 650) central to the company's growth push. The company has also started delivering its first electric motorcycle, the Flying Flea C6.
analysis.plain_terms: Royal Enfield just had its best-ever quarter for bike sales, and profit grew a healthy 21% - so the core business looks fine on the surface. But there's a real tension: most of that volume comes from smaller, sub-350cc bikes where tax just got cheaper, while the pricier bikes the company is betting on for future growth just got a lot more expensive under the new 40% GST slab. Meanwhile, the commercial-vehicle arm (VECV) grew volumes too, but its profit margin shrank because costs rose faster than prices. And despite all this, the stock has barely moved over the past year and has badly lagged its closest listed peer, TVS Motor, over the past three and five years - so the market isn't fully rewarding the operating numbers.
analysis.quarters: Q1 FY27 (June quarter): consolidated revenue ₹6,632 cr, up 31.5% YoY; EBITDA ₹1,591 cr, up 32.3% YoY with margin roughly flat YoY near 24%; PAT ₹1,463 cr, up 21.3% YoY. Royal Enfield sold a record 332,940 units, up 27% YoY, with international revenue crossing ₹1,000 cr for the first time. VECV (commercial vehicles) sold a record 24,815 vehicles, up 14.8% YoY, and revenue rose 16.6%, but EBITDA margin there slipped from about 9.2% to 8.4% as input costs rose - management flagged 4-4.5% input cost inflation as an ongoing risk. Management described the quarter as 'exceptional' and approved a new ₹1,225 cr plant in Tada, Andhra Pradesh to add capacity by FY29-30. Q2 FY27 numbers are not yet out (due 28 October 2026), so this quarter's trend on the >350cc GST impact is unverified.
analysis.performance_read: The stock trades at ₹6,959.5, about 14.1% below its February 2026 peak of ₹8,105.12. The only corporate action in its history is a 10:1 stock split in August 2020 - no demerger or spin-off - so this drawdown is a genuine price move, not a chart artifact. Over 1 year the stock is up a modest 2.15%, beating the Nifty's -13.08% but well behind peer TVS Motor's 9.92%. That gap widens further out: over 3 years the stock is up 112.81% versus TVS's 153.1%, and over 5 years it is up 186.15% versus TVS's 572.3%. So while Eicher has comfortably beaten the broad index at every horizon, it has significantly and increasingly lagged the one peer most investors compare it against - that's the uncomfortable part of an otherwise solid-looking record.
analysis.valuation_read: P/E estimates across sources range from about 32.9x to 36.1x (treat as a range, not a single number, given differing TTM windows). That's broadly in line with, or slightly below, the stock's own long-run average band of roughly 31.7x-38.7x. Why it commands this multiple: ROE of 23.9-25.2%, ROCE of 30.5-32.9%, and a near debt-free balance sheet give it a quality premium over most auto peers. Whether that multiple is actually cheap depends on whether 20%+ volume growth and ~24% EBITDA margins hold up now that the 40% GST slab has made the premium (>350cc) bikes it is counting on for growth meaningfully more expensive.
analysis.growth_read: Volume-led, not margin-led, in the latest reported quarter: Royal Enfield units grew 27% YoY and revenue grew faster than EBITDA margin expanded (margin was roughly flat YoY near 24%), so the growth is coming from more bikes sold rather than financial engineering. VECV also grew volumes (+14.8%) but margin compressed as costs rose faster than price realisation - a sign that growth there is currently being partly eaten by input costs rather than being margin-led either way.
analysis.health_read: Profitability metrics are strong - ROE 23.9-25.2%, ROCE 30.5-32.9% - and the company is described as almost debt-free, with gross borrowings of only about ₹296 cr as of March 2026 per Screener (not independently cross-verified beyond that one source). Exact free cash flow and cash-conversion figures were not verified - check on Screener. Given the high margins and low debt, the more relevant risk here is business risk - input cost inflation and the GST-driven shift in demand between bike categories - rather than financial or balance-sheet risk.
analysis.ownership_read: Promoters held 49.02% as of the September 2026 quarter, unchanged, with 0% pledged - a clean ownership picture. Foreign institutional holding has been declining for three straight quarters (26.77% to 25.52% to 24.03%) while domestic institutional holding has risen correspondingly (14.73% to 15.97% to 17.61%) - a steady rotation from foreign to domestic institutions worth watching. The largest disclosed holders are diversified funds - SBI Mutual Fund, HDFC AMC, Vanguard, BlackRock - and there is no marquee individual or concentrated investor on the register.
strengths: Royal Enfield posted a record 332,940 units sold in Q1 FY27, up 27% YoY
Consolidated PAT grew 21.3% YoY to ₹1,463 cr with EBITDA margin holding near 24%
ROE of 23.9-25.2% and ROCE of 30.5-32.9% alongside 0% promoter pledging and minimal debt
GST cut to 18% on sub-350cc bikes, which make up the bulk of Royal Enfield's volume, is a tailwind heading into the festive season
watchpoints: GST on motorcycles above 350cc raised to a flat 40%, directly affecting the premium models (Himalayan 450, Interceptor, Super Meteor, new Bullet 650) the company is relying on for growth
VECV's EBITDA margin compressed from about 9.2% to 8.4% in Q1 FY27 on rising input costs
Stock has meaningfully lagged peer TVS Motor over 3 years (+112.8% vs +153.1%) and 5 years (+186.2% vs +572.3%) despite beating the Nifty at every horizon
The new Flying Flea electric motorcycle line has no verified revenue or volume contribution yet
analysis.one_thing: The Q2 FY27 results due 28 October 2026 will show whether Royal Enfield's record volume momentum held and, crucially, whether the 40% GST on above-350cc bikes has already dented demand or margins in the premium segment the company's growth story depends on.
analysis.data_notes: Q1 FY27 results, the July 2026 dividend record date, promoter shareholding/pledge data, and the GST rate changes on motorcycles were cross-checked across multiple independent sources with no conflicts. The P/E figure (32.9x-36.1x) and historical average P/E band showed spread across sources depending on the TTM window used, so both are presented as ranges per policy on conflicting sources. Royal Enfield's average selling price, the precise net-cash rupee figure, and free cash flow were not independently verified - check on Screener. Q2 FY27 results were not yet published as of this report's date (due 28 October 2026).
